user_goal: Make the tracked Plotkeeper release-contract pointer hash platform-stable across CRLF and LF working trees, with guard and server verifier parity proof, without changing release scope or performing any operational mutation.

authority.verbatim_text: Fix cross-platform pointer hash blocker. RELEASE_CONTRACT currently binds raw working-tree SHA causing CRLF/LF divergence (Windows d4dee6..., Git/Linux 728311...). Change pointer/guard/server to platform-stable canonical JSON contract hash (or raw Git blob semantics consistently) and add CRLF/LF parity regression proving guard+verifier agree. Append-only successor contract if required, exact scope only. No commit/push/install. Full/focused tests, diff check, concise handoff, then stop.

baseline.protection_evidence: Exact current release-surface head after the prior release-contract selection fix; no operational action is authorized.
baseline.selection_reason: The delegated repair is limited to cross-platform canonical hashing of the existing tracked pointer target and its parity proof.

resources: Disposable temporary contract fixtures and in-memory CRLF/LF byte variants only.
semantic_changes: Hash the parsed contract's canonical JSON representation for pointer verification, independent of newline encoding.
Require host guard and server verifier to accept equivalent CRLF/LF contract bytes and reject altered canonical content.
Preserve the designated contract path, ID, release requirements, workflow configuration, and all release behavior.

paths: any path not explicitly listed under allowed.paths
semantic_changes: No release, merge, push, install, restart, deployment, listener, connector, ledger, UI, dependency, or user-project mutation.
No raw working-tree newline, filesystem mtime, filename ordering, environment override, or alternate contract may alter release authority.
No test may touch an installed service, live listener, or user data.

invariants: Equivalent LF and CRLF representations of the designated contract resolve to the same canonical hash in guard and verifier.
Canonical content changes, pointer ID/path changes, malformed pointers, and non-release contracts fail closed.
The designated v0.1.7 public-release contract and exact pointer path remain unchanged except for the hash representation.
No commit, push, install, restart, deployment, or live-service mutation occurs.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: Guard and server verifier accept equivalent LF and CRLF contract bytes using one platform-stable canonical JSON hash.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Windows/Linux newline differences cause false rejection or guard/verifier disagreement.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: Tracked release pointer, host guard, and server verifier

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: Canonical content tampering and pointer/contract identity mismatch fail closed.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Raw-byte normalization masks semantic content changes or allows a non-release contract.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: Disposable contract fixtures and release decision paths

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: Only the authorized hash, pointer, test, contract, and checkpoint surfaces change and all validation passes.

proof_requirements.claim: Guard and server verifier produce and consume identical canonical JSON contract hashes for LF and CRLF fixtures.
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Focused guard and verifier CRLF/LF parity tests
proof_requirements.expected_observation: Both paths select the same contract for both newline encodings.

proof_requirements.claim: Semantic contract and pointer tampering fail closed after canonical hashing.
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Focused tamper and identity mismatch tests
proof_requirements.expected_observation: No release authorization is returned for altered content.

proof_requirements.claim: The bounded diff is regression-free and operationally untouched.
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Contract validation, focused/full tests, py_compile, and git diff --check
proof_requirements.expected_observation: All checks pass and no forbidden surface changes.

release_requirements.required_receipt: No release or deployment is authorized in this bounded parity repair lane.

stop_conditions: Any unexpected diff, newline-dependent behavior, failed test, contract validation failure, or diff-check failure.
Any request to commit, push, install, restart, deploy, or broaden scope without a new contract.
known_discrepancies: The prior pointer stored a raw working-tree hash, which is not portable across newline-normalizing checkouts.
